title: MWE of the v4 calculators, building on v4atoms
body:
Builds on top of !3960 by extracting Calculator-related changes from !3857. 

The idea is to have a v4 Calculator base class, so that all the supported calculators can over time be switched over to this from the current v3 Calculator class. Meanwhile, a `Version4Adaptor` wrapper already introduces a new `.evaluate` method to the v3 calculators, so that the new interface can be tested in downstream applications. EMT is used as an example for the wrapper. 

This is just a suggestion for the new API, to be updated or rewritten as suggestions and limitations appear with downstream testing. Next step: test the EMT `.evaluate` interface in dynamics applications (geometry optimization, molecular dynamics) and update as needed. 

Main components:
- calculator.py has a new independent `Calculator` class that follows the v3 class, but removes `.calculate` and all the `Calculator`-atached atoms. 
- It also has a `Version4Adaptor` that wraps a v3 calculator class for it to have a v4-style `.evaluate` method.
- A v4Adptor-wrapped EMT calculator.
- Related unit tests.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: We can probably import it from v3 as e.g. `from ase.calculators.calculator import all_properties`.

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body: all_properties are unused here, so the import could be skipped altogether. However, in the future we will need to check the v4 calculator's `all_properties`, which at the moment is just an import of what's defined in v3 calculator.py. I have left the unused import, but don't have strong feelings either way, so just let me know if you would rather `all_properties` weren't imported without use.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: OK, let's leave it at the moment :)

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: This looks also the same as v3, so we can do `from ase.calculators.calculator import equal`.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Maybe we can already annotate like `def evaluate(self, atoms, properties) -> CalculationResults:`?

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body: This is tricky - the way current v3 calculator inheritance works (and this implementation follows) is that `Calculator(BaseCalculator)` doesn't actually return any results (or here - `CalculationResults`). So a type annotation here is misleading and doesn't quite make sense without a more major redesign where `Calculator` class or child classes set up the directories less implicitly and always return results/CalculationResults. Because it's a more distinct change in logic (v3 and v4) and, I think, out of scope for this PR, I would like to leave this non-annotated here.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Possibly there was a misunderstanding. I just meant only for `evaluate`, not all methods.

Anyway, we can also leave it for the moment.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:

So far I just made a few suggestions / questions if we can import some functionalities that are the same as `ase.calculators.calculator`. We can also solve he `lint` pipeline failures, and then I think we can go ahead.

(On my side, I will once again have a look on !3960 to better align with.)

comments.author: gelzinyte
comments.body: Hi Yuji, thanks a lot for the review! I've either implemented and resolved your suggestions or left comments. I have also made some smaller unrelated improvements, so you might want to review the latest set of changes (commit c9274cc7 and later).

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:

Like !3960, we do not have to fix the v4 API so strictly for the moment, so I think the present MR is ready.
If we do not see further comments from @askhl @ajjackson @jameskermode in one or two days, let's merge, and we can go to the next step :)
